ITEM 3, AND THE WORST THING IN EITHER FILE: TWO ROWS OF ONE TABLE CONTRADICTING EACH OTHER ABOUT WHETHER A GUARD CAN FIRE. The WORLD.load_into row ended '...without it OPT's param_group_shape refusal fires on every resume of a run that ever grew (:4580-4599). That refusal is itself written against a field OPT.state_dict never says it writes -- opt/api.py::maybe_step against :273-276, and OptState declares no such field -- so the ordering constraint this row exists for currently protects a guard that cannot fire.'

EVERY CLAUSE OF THAT IS FALSE IN THE TREE AS IT STANDS. (i) opt/api.py::state_dict's docstring enumerates 'the resolved horizon, param_group_shape, and the counters' and then explains the enumeration: 'param_group_shape WAS MISSING FROM THIS ENUMERATION UNTIL 2026-09-02 (Q-OPT-4) AND load_state REFUSES ON IT. A refusal armed against a value nothing writes is untrippable'. (ii) OptState declares the field -- `param_group_shape: tuple`. (iii) opt/api.py::load_state opens 'REFUSES when saved.param_group_shape differs from the live one', and build() computes it (`shape = _param_group_shape(ordered)`) and stores it on the record. The guard fires.

AND THE CITATION WAS WRONG TOO: opt/api.py::maybe_step is not where OPT.state_dict's enumeration lives. It is another instance of the wrong-symbol family below.

WHY THIS ONE IS HIGH AND THE OTHERS ARE NOT. The OPT.load_state row SEVEN ROWS BELOW in the SAME tuple already carried the correction -- 'OPT.state_dict now declares it writes param_group_shape, which it did not, so the refusal compares against a value something produces instead of being untrippable' -- so an earlier round corrected one row and not its neighbour. A table that says both things at once about one guard is worse than either statement alone: a reader who finds the contradiction cannot tell which row was re-read, and the false half is exactly the shape the spine ranks above all others -- a mechanism declared unable to fire when it can. It is the mirror of 'armed, did not fire' for a mechanism that cannot fire, and it was standing over the ORDERING CONSTRAINT that the whole row exists to justify.

THE REPAIR keeps the ordering rationale untouched (it is correct and independent) and states that the constraint protects a guard that CAN fire -- a stronger reason for the ordering, not a weaker one -- with the old sentence quoted as what the row said until 2026-09-04 and both correct symbols (opt/api.py::state_dict, opt/api.py::load_state) named.
